title: Migrate node lifecycle to event-sourced history with legacy state adapter
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Background: The current node lifecycle is driven by ad-hoc reconciliation loops and a mutable node state blob stored in the fleet controller. Over years of incremental fixes this has created brittle corner-cases during concurrent upgrades, fast scale-ups, and graceful eviction flows. The autoscaler and capacity planner frequently need to reason about historical transitions (why a node was cordoned, when drains started, lease handoff sequences) but the information is often lost or encoded in log traces.

Goal: Replace the single mutable state model with an append-only, event-sourced node history and introduce a compatibility adapter that exposes the same state machine API consumed by existing subsystems. The event store will be the canonical source of truth for lifecycle transitions; read models will be built to serve the autoscaler, capacity planner, and dashboard queries. The compatibility adapter lets us incrementally migrate consumers while keeping runtime behavior stable.

Scope:
- Implement a small event schema (NodeCreated, LeaseAcquired, Cordon, DrainStarted, DrainCompleted, EvictionRequested, LeaseReleased, NodeDeleted).
- Durable append-only store backed by Postgres (pg_eventstore table) with compacting TTL for older events.
- Read model service to project current node state and recent transition windows for autoscaler fast-paths.
- Compatibility adapter (NodeStateAdapter) that answers existing GetNodeState/GetLease API surface via read-model snapshots.
- Migration tool to backfill events from reconciler traces and existing node annotations.
- Feature flag gated rollout (node-lifecycle-events) and gradual switch per-cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
- All lifecycle transitions are written as events in the new store for clusters in the rollout group.
- NodeStateAdapter returns identical states to legacy controller within 1s for 99th percentile of queries during rollout tests.
- Autoscaler queries switch to read-model endpoints with no regressions in throughput/latency (<=5% p99 increase allowed during warmup).
- Migration backfill completes for a test cluster and produces identical read-models to current state.
- End-to-end e2e tests for cordon/drain/eviction flows passing in CI.

Risks & mitigations:
- Performance: event write latency could affect reconciliation loops. Mitigate by batching writes and async fsync during warmup; fall back to legacy path on write failures.
- Storage growth: event retention must be bounded. Implement compaction jobs and snapshotting of read-model state every N events.
- Consistency: eventually consistent read-models can cause transient autoscaler decisions. Mitigate by adding short-lived strong-read path for critical queries (lease handoff) and by keeping legacy path available until safe switchover.
- Rollback complexity: keep feature flag control and an operator-run rollback job that drains new events into an archival table for post-mortem.

Migration plan:
1) Spike & PoC: event schema + minimal pg_eventstore and a test read-model (completed).
2) Implement event writers in reconciler and node controller; start writing to store behind feature flag.
3) Backfill tool to convert annotations/logs into events for rollout clusters.
4) Stand up NodeStateAdapter and switch non-critical consumers (console, debug tools).
5) Gradually migrate autoscaler and capacity planner; run canary traffic and compare decisions.
6) Full switch for cluster pools after 2 weeks of stable canary metrics.

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Writes/sec, event store latency (p50/p95/p99)
- Read-model staleness distribution (lag seconds)
- Autoscaler decision divergence rate vs legacy (should be <1.5% during warmup)
- Reduction in incident tickets related to node-state races (target 70% reduction over 3 months)

Follow-ups / future work:
- Extend events for more detailed resource-level transitions (GPU drain phases)
- Expose a time-travel debug UI in Console using the event store
- Evaluate moving from Postgres to a write-optimized store if write volume grows beyond thresholds
comments: 2025-03-03 - Spike complete: PoC used pg_eventstore table + minimal writer in controller. Observed median write latency 7ms under synthetic load. Notes: need batching to get steady p99 under 50ms.
2025-03-05 - Design review with autoscaler owners @Liam O'Connor and @Priya Singh. Action: add strong-read path for lease transfer queries and a reconciliation guard to avoid double-eviction.
2025-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1842 (draft) - adds event writer scaffolding. Requesting review from @sara-kim (db), @mkol (autoscaler).
2025-03-11 - Backfill spike: wrote 48k events for a single test-pool from reconciler traces. Migration tool needs heuristics to dedupe overlapping events from repeated reconciliation runs.

2025-03-12 - Ran canary in staging: NodeStateAdapter returned correct state for 99.8% of nodes within 500ms. Two issues discovered: missing LeaseReleased events when controllers crash; mitigation: add on-start reconciliation to emit synthetic release if lease older than TTL.
